No claim here establishes who was responsible for any change, or whether any change was improper.", "key_points": ["A record states that Nima Brack submitted 48 overtime hours for the weekend dispatch team on 4 March 2026. [C001]", "A record states the agreed overtime rate for this synthetic team is $24 per hour. [C002]", "A record states the original 48 hours total $1,152 and the edited 30 hours total $720, a $432 difference. The editor is not identified in the record, and the verifier did not establish the editor's identity. [C003]", "The packet states six hours were restored for $144, leaving 12 hours or $288 in dispute. [C004, C028]", "Ledger entries dated 2026-04-10 record L001 as paid overtime of 30 hours at $720.00, L002 as repaid overtime of 6 hours at $144.00, L003 as disputed overtime of 12 hours at $288.00, and a packet total of $1152.00. [C022, C031, C032, C033]", "A correction is recorded with the reason 'budget alignment', and employee approvals are blank. [C006]", "Nima Brack's email is described as alleging that PERSON_1 PERSON_1 removed 18 overtime hours from approved timesheets without employee sign-off. This is an uncorroborated allegation, and its timing is inferred rather than stated in the source. [C007]", "A payroll memo attributed to PERSON_1 PERSON_1 states that all 18 removed hours were duplicate clock entries. This conflicts with the allegation about the same hours. The passages do not establish which account is accurate. [C007, C008]", "A review status document states that in early April PERSON_1 authorized repayment of six of the removed overtime hours. The date anchor is uncertain. [C009]", "After the audit, Nima Brack exported the timesheet revision history, and a receipt dated 10 April 2026 records a preservation action. [C010, C025]", "The audit date does not appear on the calendar extract. No signed audit report was available for the packet, and the signed audit report and an independent copy of the source register are still requested. [C011, C012, C023]", "Gate scans and loading manifests cover all three shifts, but the record notes that a gate scan does not itself establish paid working time. [C005]", "A chat on 9 March 2026 records the following Monday challenge to missing overtime, a request to keep the original and the edit history, and a direction from PERSON_1 PERSON_1 to keep the matter in the review queue. [C016, C017, C018]", "In the same chat, a participant identified only as [REDACTED] said they had the earlier copy and that the totals did not match yet, and agreed to keep the original and send it after shift. [C019, C026]", "A 4 March 2026 email about clock corrections for pay period 06 was sent from a redacted sender to PERSON_1, and a 6 March 2026 email in the same thread was sent by Nima Brack. [C020, C021]", "Nima Brack's signature block gives the role Review coordinator, and the record states that the authorization and settlement fields are separate. [C029, C030]", "A statement in the packet says no conclusions should be reached until the source records are checked. The speaker is not identified. [C027]", "Reporter account, unverified: the reporter states they watched the total drop after approval and kept both exports. [C013, C035]", "Reporter account, unverified: the reporter states the hours were scheduled loading shifts rather than accidental double punches, while also stating they cannot speak for every break taken. [C014, C024]", "Reporter account, unverified: the reporter states that people asked them why their payslips were short, and that they reconcile dispatch hours before the pay file closes.
